osservatorio.riga: As an educator working with unaccompanied foreign minors, I saw that integration succeeds or fails mostly on how the reception centres manage it. That is where the causes lie; looking only at the symptoms, petty crime and marginalisation, feeds extremism instead of improving reception.
osservatorio.ruolo: Personal project · conceived and built by me · open source
compiti: Python pipeline over 18,058 contracts from 2015 to 2025, from three ANAC datasets joined on the CIG code.
CPV-code and text filter to isolate reception services, refined after feedback from a social worker.
pdfplumber parser for about 90 ministry reports on unaccompanied foreign minors.

A thesis of mine disproved by the data: in 2024 direct awards seemed to soar, but from that year ANAC also records contracts under €40,000, almost all of them direct. The site shows both series, with and without those contracts.
Static Next.js site with 116 pages, LCP from 11 to 1 second; monthly update driven by GitHub Actions.
osservatorio.strumenti: Python · pdfplumber · Next.js 16 · React 19 · TypeScript · GitHub Actions · Vercel

violenza.riga: An observatory on violence against men in Italy, which nobody measures systematically today: verified public data and its context, a guide for those who suffer it or are accused, and support services. Non-commercial.
violenza.ruolo: Personal project · conceived, designed and built by me
compiti: ISTAT SDI-SSD table 2014-2024, ISTAT regional boundaries and a hand-compiled CSV of services, versioned in the repository; three Python scripts using only the standard library turn them into JSON (the xlsx read with zipfile and XML, the shapefile simplified into SVG paths).

The services script runs before every build and stops it if a required field, an https source or a valid verification date is missing; it warns when a service has not been rechecked for over six months. Two GitHub Actions workflows open an issue every three months for the services and once a year for the new ISTAT table.
3D scenes on a 2D canvas with the isometric projection computed by hand, no libraries, always next to the exact value; on mobile and with prefers-reduced-motion they stay still.
Regional map and 2014-2024 time series in hand-written SVG, with a timeline; long content in tabs on mobile and sliders on desktop, always present in the HTML.
A help column fixed on every page (112, helplines, index), a bottom bar on mobile, a "Leave now" button. No cookies, no tracking; light and dark theme with no flash on load.
Every figure with source, year and method; where data is missing it says "n/a", never 0. Data downloadable as CSV, Dataset JSON-LD, Lighthouse accessibility 100.
violenza.strumenti: Python · Next.js 16 · React 19 · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS 4 · GitHub Actions · Vercel

meta.descrizione: Before websites, olive oil: a professional farmer in Chiaramonte Gulfi, cold-pressed oil milled within twenty-four hours, sold across Italy and Europe.

olio.attacco: I made olive oil with my family from the time I was a child, and later as a profession: a professional farmer with my own land in Chiaramonte Gulfi. Oil cold-pressed within twenty-four hours of the harvest, sold across Italy and Europe.
storia: Chiaramonte Gulfi lies in the Hyblaean Mountains, in the province of Ragusa: old olive trees, trunks split open by time, red earth. My land was there, and my oil came only from those trees.
The harvest was a family job. Nets spread under the trees, poles among the branches, olives in crates; my mother on the truck bed, stacking the day's load.

I followed the strictest methods, because the quality of an oil is decided in a few hours: milling within twenty-four hours of the harvest, cold extraction, no shortcuts. Then the oil left for Italy and Europe, and I followed that too.

metodo.testo: From the trees on the farm: nets spread on the ground, poles among the branches, olives gathered into crates.
From tree to mill in less than a day: the longer an olive waits, the more the oil loses aroma and picks up defects.
Crushing and pressing at low temperature, so the oil keeps its aromas and polyphenols. Freshly made, it comes out green and cloudy.
Bottled and shipped to those who chose it, in Italy and abroad. I handled the sales as well.

olio.videoTitolo: In the grove and at the mill
olio.perche: Today I build websites. For an olive oil company I know what to tell and how to sell it: the grove, the mill, the tight timing of the harvest; product pages for each oil, a shop that ships across Italy and Europe, visibility on Google for people looking for oil. I know the work as a producer and as a developer: I can build the site, the shop and the copy.

vignette: A text is a lazy mechanism that needs the reader's intervention to come alive.
Marco comes home. “Where have you been?” Marina exclaims darkly.
The text doesn't tell us that Marco and Marina are in the same room, nor that Marina is talking to Marco.
And it doesn't tell us that “darkly” means Marina is furious.
We readers add that information: that is how the text is completed.
On its own the text doesn't work: it works with the meaning the reader adds to it.
